title: Jellied Russian Buckwheat Pilaf
description: A traditional Russian dish featuring buckwheat, dried fruit, and a tangy nuka-pickle sauce, perfect for a brunch mood.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine buckwheat groats and water; bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
While buckwheat cooks, melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Stir in nuka-pickle juice, honey, apple cider vinegar, and ground ginger; bring to a simmer.
Cook for 2-3 minutes or until sauce thickens slightly.
Fluff cooked buckwheat with a fork and stir in chopped dried apricots and cranberries.
Pour sauce over buckwheat mixture and stir to combine.
Transfer pilaf to a serving dish and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
To serve, slice into squares and garnish with additional dried fruit, if desired.
